newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper hits 6-mth low on widespread selling.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper hits 6-mth low on widespread selling.

text.p: COMEX copper fell sharply at midday, crushing trendline support in September at 102.50 cents a lb, triggering sell stops from most sectors in the market and sending prices to their lowest level in six months, dealers said.

Managed funds, commission houses and commercial dealers hit the market with a a combination of liquidation and fresh selling, according to James Quinn, commodity commentator for A.G. Edwards, feeling the weight from both key chart points and weak fundamentals.
At 1224 EDT, the December contract was 100.70 cents a lb, down 1.90 cents from Thursday. September was 101.20 cents a lb, down 2.60 cents. The spot month was 101.00 cents a lb, down 2.60 cents.
The London Metal Exchange flipped into a contango market for the first time in 10 months under the weight of warehouse stocks that have been steadily increasing for the last two months.
"We hit some key sell stops at 102.50 cents a lb," Quinn said. "The stocks are what most of the market is focusing on. Both LME and COMEX stocks are increasing. Demand is pretty quiet."
The September downtrend dates back to July 30 and provided support at 102.50 cents. "A lot of stops were lurking just underneath there."
LME warehouse stocks increased 4,575 tonnes to 260,875 tonnes, the highest level in 11 months. COMEX stocks have increased 2,712 short tons in the last two trading days to 36,581 tons.
The LME cash-to-three-month spread is bid at a $2 contango, which would appear to reflect ample supplies.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
